How does wind speed affect a turbine's power?

The faster the wind blows, the more electricity a turbine can make!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakaapekto ang bilis ng hangin sa turbina?

Kapag mas mabilis ang hangin, mas maraming kuryente ang nagagawa ng turbina!

Unsaon pag-apekto sa kusog sa hangin ang turbine?

Kung mas paspas ang hangin, mas daghang kuryente ang mahimo sa turbine!

copy.en: Spines, thorns, hard shells — some animals wear built-in armor. These physical defenses keep predators from being able to eat them at all.
copy.tl: Tinik, tinutuktok, matigas na balat — may mga hayop na may built-in na baluti. Ginagamit nila ito para hindi sila makain ng mga predator.
copy.bis: Tunok, gahi nga balhibo o kabhang — ang uban mananap adunay natural nga hinagiban. Kini nga pisikal nga depensa nagpugong sa mga predator sa pagkaon kanila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Load-bearing walls carry the weight of floors and the roof above.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses weight and structural support but does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or explain how gravity affects materials/objects in predictable ways. It is about building safety, not the force of gravity itself.

copy.en: Load-bearing walls carry the weight of floors and the roof above. Never remove them without first supporting that weight another way!
copy.tl: Ang mga load-bearing walls ay nagdadala ng timbang ng mga sahig at bubong sa itaas. Huwag alisin ang mga ito nang walang ibang suporta!
copy.bis: Ang mga load-bearing walls nagdala sa timbang sa mga sahig ug bubong sa ibabaw. Ayaw kuhaa kining mga walla kung walay laing suporta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Styrofoam is a great insulator because it's full of tiny air pockets!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pockets and insulation but does not explain conduction or convection using the particle model, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Styrofoam is a great insulator because it's full of tiny air pockets! This keeps your food hot or cold for a longer time.
copy.tl: Magandang insulator ang styrofoam dahil puno ito ng maliliit na air pockets! Kaya nananatiling mainit o malamig ang pagkain nang mas matagal.
copy.bis: Maayong insulator ang styrofoam kay puno kini og gagmayng air pockets! Mao nga mas dugay nga magpabilin nga mainit o malamig ang pagkain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It turns directly from a solid into a gas. This cool process is called sublimation!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches sublimation, a change of state not listed in the competency (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation). It also does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It turns directly from a solid into a gas. This cool process is called sublimation!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a solid-to-gas change, but the competency focuses on temperature-driven changes such as solid to liquid to gas. Sublimation is not an example given and the card does not explain the role of temperature in the change.

copy.en:
Did you know camphor can skip being a liquid?

Yes! It turns directly from a solid into a gas. This cool process is called sublimation!
copy.tl:
Alam mo bang ang alkampor ay pwedeng lumaktaw sa pagiging likido?

Oo! Diretsong nagiging singaw ito mula sa solido. Ang prosesong ito ay tinatawag na sublimasyon!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang kamper pwede maglukso sa pagkahimong likido?

Oo! Diretsa kini moalisngaw gikan sa gahi nga porma. Kini nga proseso gitawag og sublimation!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In sublimation, a solid turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sublimation, a change of state, but G6-M-1 specifically requires describing melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation using diagrams/flowcharts. Sublimation is not among the listed processes, and the card uses no diagrams or flowcharts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In sublimation, a solid turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: G7-M-5 requires explaining changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes for solid→liquid→vapor and vapor→liquid→solid. The card only mentions sublimation (solid→gas) and does not address particle arrangement or energy changes, nor the specified transitions.

copy.en: In sublimation, a solid turns straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first! Dry ice "smokes," and mothballs slowly shrink until they completely disappear.
copy.tl: Sa sublimation, ang solid ay direktang nagiging gas nang hindi muna nagiging likido! Ang dry ice ay parang umuusok, at ang mothballs ay unti-unting lumiliit hanggang mawala.
copy.bis: Sa sublimation, ang solid direktang mahimong gas nga dili una mahimong likido! Ang dry ice daw nag-aso, ug ang mothballs hinay-hinayng mokunhod hangtod mawala.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sublimation is when a solid changes straight into a gas without becoming liquid first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sublimation, which is not among the changes of state named in the competency (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation), and it does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sublimation is when a solid changes straight into a gas without becoming liquid first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on temperature-driven changes such as solid to liquid to gas; sublimation is a solid-to-gas change but is not the solid-to-liquid-to-gas sequence described, and the card does not address temperature as the cause.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sublimation is when a solid changes straight into a gas without becoming liquid first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines sublimation but does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: Sublimation is when a solid changes straight into a gas without becoming liquid first, just like dry ice!
copy.tl: Ang sublimation ay pagbabago ng solid diretso sa gas nang hindi muna nagiging likido, tulad ng dry ice!
copy.bis: Ang sublimation mao ang pagbalhin sa solid diretso ngadto sa gas nga dili una mahimong likido, sama sa dry ice!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Right below the topsoil is the subsoil!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the subsoil layer and its color/decayed-plant content. It does not explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals, so it does not directly support G5-E-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This layer looks more reddish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions color but concerns soil layers, not observing or collecting rocks or comparing rock features such as texture, color, and grain crystal size. It does not directly support G5-E-2.

copy.en: Right below the topsoil is the subsoil! This layer looks more reddish and has fewer decayed plants hiding inside.
copy.tl: Nasa ilalim ng topsoil ang subsoil! Ang layer na ito ay mas mapula at may mas kaunting bulok na halaman.
copy.bis: Sa ilalom sa topsoil naa ang subsoil! Kini nga layer mas mapula ug mas gamay ang nadunot nga mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some species are divided into smaller groups called subspecies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the concept of subspecies, a taxonomic rank below species, but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, fungi, bacteria). It is only tangentially related to classification.

copy.en:
What is a subspecies?

Some species are divided into smaller groups called subspecies, which differ a little by region and sometimes get a third word added to their name.
copy.tl:
Ano ang subspecies?

Ang ilang species ay nahahati sa mas maliliit na grupong tinatawag na subspecies, na may bahagyang pagkakaiba ayon sa rehiyon, at minsan may idinaragdag na ikatlong salita sa pangalan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang subspecies?

Ang ubang species nabahin ngadto sa mas gagmay nga grupo nga gitawag og subspecies, nga gamayng lahi sumala sa rehiyon, ug usahay gidugangan og ikatulong pulong ang ngalan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Suckers are upright shoots that grow from buds at the base of a plant's stem, and banana, bamboo, and pineapple reproduce this way.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes suckers as a mode of plant reproduction (vegetative propagation), which is an example of asexual reproduction. However, the competency requires differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction based on number of parents and offspring similarity. The card does not address these criteria or contrast asexual with sexual reproduction, so it only provides related background rather than directly teaching the differentiation.

copy.en: Suckers are upright shoots that grow from buds at the base of a plant's stem, and banana, bamboo, and pineapple reproduce this way.
copy.tl: Ang suckers ay mga tuwid na shoot na tumutubo mula sa buds sa base ng stem ng halaman, at ganito dumami ang saging, kawayan, at pinya.
copy.bis: Ang suckers mga tul-id nga shoot nga motubo gikan sa buds sa base sa stem sa tanom, ug ingon ani mosanay ang saging, kawayan, ug pinya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sweet juice is stored inside its stalk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the stalk (stem) but does not describe its role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It focuses on sugar storage, not the transport/absorption function required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sweet juice is stored inside its stalk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how plant organs (leaf, stem, roots) work together as the transport system
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes that juice is stored in the stalk. It does not describe how leaf, stem, and roots work together as a transport system, so it does not directly support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sugarcane is actually a tall grass!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies sugarcane as a grass and mentions the stalk, but it does not describe the purpose of specialized structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. The stalk is not presented as a specialized structure with a purpose.

copy.en: Sugarcane is actually a tall grass! Sweet juice is stored inside its stalk, and that juice is what becomes sugar.
copy.tl: Damo pala ang tubo, isang matangkad na damo! May matamis na katas ito sa loob ng tangkay, at dito nagmumula ang asukal.
copy.bis: Sagbot diay ang tubo, taas nga sagbot! Adunay tam-is nga duga sulod sa lawas niini, ug gikan niini ang asukal.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The chemical formula for the sweet table sugar we love to eat is C12H22O11

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The chemical formula for the sweet table sugar we love to eat is C12H22O11
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical name of some common covalent compounds, including water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and ammonia (NH3)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the formula and name of sucrose, a covalent compound, but the competency requires writing chemical formulas and names of common covalent compounds including water, carbon dioxide, and ammonia. Sucrose is not among the listed examples, and the card does not teach how to write formulas or names generally.

copy.en:
What is the chemical formula for the sweet table sugar we love to eat?

The chemical formula for the sweet table sugar we love to eat is C12H22O11, also known as sucrose!
copy.tl:
Ano ang kemikal na pormula ng matamis na asukal sa mesa na gusto natin?

Ang kemikal na pormula ng matamis na asukal sa mesa na gusto natin ay C12H22O11, na kilala bilang sucrose!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kemikal nga pormula sa tamis nga asukal sa lamesa nga atong ganahan?

Ang kemikal nga pormula sa tamis nga asukal sa lamesa nga atong ganahan kay C12H22O11, nga nailhan nga sucrose!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Table sugar is a compound, and when heated, it breaks down into carbon and water, showing it is made of different elements.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Table sugar is a compound, and when heated, it breaks down into carbon and water, showing it is made of different elements.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: develop a timeline for the historical background of the development of the current Atomic Model that identifies tiny particles as atoms
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the composition of a compound, not about the historical development of the atomic model or a timeline of atomic theory. It does not support the competency's focus on the historical background of the atomic model.

copy.en: Table sugar is a compound, and when heated, it breaks down into carbon and water, showing it is made of different elements.
copy.tl: Ang table sugar ay isang compound, at kapag pinainit, ito ay nasisira at nagiging carbon at tubig, na nagpapakita na ito ay gawa sa iba't ibang element.
copy.bis: Ang table sugar usa ka compound, ug kung initon, kini mabungkag ug mahimong carbon ug tubig, nga nagpakita nga kini hinimo sa lain-laing mga element.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sugar solution cannot conduct electricity because sugar dissolves as intact molecules, not as ions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a property of a solution (electrical conductivity) but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It shares the broad topic of matter but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's definition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sugar solution cannot conduct electricity because sugar dissolves as intact molecules, not as ions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan simple scientific investigations in answering questions, such as 'Do gases (like air) or liquids (like water) have mass?', using appropriate simple science equipment, such as a balance, and a thermometer, with appropriate units
assignedReviews.reason: The card makes a factual statement about sugar solution conductivity; it does not involve planning a scientific investigation, using equipment like a balance or thermometer, or addressing whether gases/liquids have mass. No direct support for the investigation-planning competency.

copy.en: A sugar solution cannot conduct electricity because sugar dissolves as intact molecules, not as ions, so there are no charged particles free to carry the current.
copy.tl: Ang sugar solution ay hindi makapagpadala ng kuryente dahil ang asukal ay natutunaw bilang buong molecules, hindi bilang ions, kaya walang charged particles na malayang magdadala ng current.
copy.bis: Ang sugar solution dili makapadala og kuryente tungod kay ang asukar matunaw isip tibuok nga molecules, dili isip ions, busa walay charged particles nga gawasnon nga magdala sa current.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun looks way bigger and brighter than other stars just because it is the absolute closest star to us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card only addresses the Sun's apparent size/brightness due to proximity, not its actual overall characteristics such as composition, actual size, or the main energy it radiates.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun looks way bigger and brighter than other stars just because it is the absolute closest star to us!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun as a star but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition.

copy.en: The Sun looks way bigger and brighter than other stars just because it is the absolute closest star to us!
copy.tl: Mukhang mas malaki at maliwanag ang Araw kaysa sa ibang bituin dahil siya lang ang pinakamalapit sa atin!
copy.bis: Morag mas dako ug mas hayag ang Adlaw kaysa ubang bituon tungod lang kay siya ang labing duol kanato!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is about 150 million kilometers away from Earth.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the Sun–Earth distance. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or discuss their features or composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How far away is the Sun from Earth?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun but does not involve guided observation or description of natural objects in the sky, nor does it describe the Sun's appearance or behavior. It only gives a distance fact, which is not the focus of the competency.

copy.en:
How far away is the Sun from Earth?

The Sun is super far! It is about 150 million kilometers away from Earth.
copy.tl:
Gaano kalayo ang Araw mula sa Lupa?

Sobrang layo ng Araw! Humigit-kumulang 150 milyong kilometro ang layo nito mula sa Lupa.
copy.bis:
Unsa kahalayo ang Adlaw gikan sa Yuta?

Layo kaayo ang Adlaw! Mga 150 ka milyon nga kilometro ang gilay-on niini gikan sa Yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves stay open in daytime to catch sunlight — the tree uses that light energy to make its own food.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that leaves catch sunlight and use light energy to make food. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials or products, which are the core actions of G8-L-9. The content is a simple, early-elementary statement about sunlight and food-making, not direct instructional support for the Grade 8 competency.

copy.en:
Why do leaves stay open by day?

Leaves stay open in daytime to catch sunlight — the tree uses that light energy to make its own food.
copy.tl:
Bakit bukas ang dahon sa araw?

Nakabukas ang dahon sa araw para makuha ang sikat ng araw, na ginagamit ng puno sa paggawa ng sariling pagkain.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga abli ang dahon kon adlaw?

Abli ang dahon kon adlaw aron makuha ang silaw sa adlaw, nga gigamit sa kahoy sa paghimo sa iyang kaugalingong pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunlight zooms to Earth in just eight minutes! But light from other stars takes years to reach us because they are super far away.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the travel time of light from the Sun and other stars, but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or cover their features and composition. It only shares a fact about light travel time, which is not part of the competency.

copy.en: Sunlight zooms to Earth in just eight minutes! But light from other stars takes years to reach us because they are super far away.
copy.tl: Ang liwanag ng Araw ay umaabot sa Earth sa loob lang ng walong minuto! Pero ang liwanag ng ibang bituin ay tumatagal ng ilang taon dahil sobrang layo nila.
copy.bis: Ang kahayag sa Adlaw moabot sa Yuta sulod lang sa walo ka minuto! Apan ang kahayag sa ubang bituon moabot og pipila ka tuig kay sobra ka layo kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it has so much mass, its pull is super strong!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun's gravitational pull but does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or describe its predictable effects on objects on Earth, which is the focus of G5-F-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Sun holds about 99% of all the mass in the solar system!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives one fact about the Sun's mass but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or describe their main features and composition as required by G5-E-11.

copy.en:
Why is the Sun's pull so strong?

The Sun holds about 99% of all the mass in the solar system! Only a tiny bit is left for the planets. Because it has so much mass, its pull is super strong!
copy.tl:
Bakit napakalakas ng hila ng Araw?

Hawak ng Araw ang mga 99% ng lahat ng mass sa solar system! Konti lang ang natitira sa mga planeta. Dahil napakaraming mass niya, napakalakas ng hila nito sa lahat!
copy.bis:
Ngano kusog kaayo ang birik sa Adlaw?

Gikuptan sa Adlaw ang mga 99% sa tanang mass sa solar system! Gamay ra ang nahibilin sa mga planeta. Tungod kay daghan kaayo ang mass niini, kusog kaayo ang birik niini sa tanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Since it's gas, its middle (equator) spins faster than the parts near its poles.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun is gas, which touches on composition, but the main content is differential rotation, not the overall characteristics (composition, size, main energy) that G4-E-7 asks students to describe. The gas mention is incidental and does not directly support describing the Sun's overall characteristics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Does the Sun spin at the same speed everywhere?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: G3-E-7 is about observing and recording how and when the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars move across the sky (apparent motion). The card discusses the Sun's internal rotation speed differences, not its apparent motion across the sky. This is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Does the Sun spin at the same speed everywhere?

Nope! Since it's gas, its middle (equator) spins faster than the parts near its poles.
copy.tl:
Pare-pareho ba ang bilis ng pag-ikot ng Araw?

Hindi! Dahil gas ito, mas mabilis umikot ang gitna (equator) nito kaysa sa mga bahaging malapit sa poles.
copy.bis:
Managsama ba ang katulin sa pagtuyok sa Adlaw?

Dili! Tungod kay gas kini, mas paspas motuyok ang tunga (equator) niini kaysa sa mga bahin nga duol sa poles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunspots and solar flares change in an 11-year cycle!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some of the overall characteristics of the Sun, such as its composition, its size, and the main energy it radiates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the solar activity cycle (sunspots, flares, magnetic shifts) but does not address the Sun's composition, size, or main radiated energy, which are the specific characteristics in G4-E-7.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sunspots and solar flares change in an 11-year cycle!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Sun as a celestial object but does not support guided observation or description of natural objects in the sky; it focuses on the sunspot cycle rather than observing or describing the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars.

copy.en: Sunspots and solar flares change in an 11-year cycle! The Sun's magnetic force shifts, creating busy times with many bursts and quiet times with almost none.
copy.tl: Nagbabago ang sunspots at solar flares sa 11-year cycle! Lumilipat ang magnetic force ng Araw, kaya may panahong maraming sabog at panahong halos wala.
copy.bis: Nagausab ang sunspots ug solar flare sa 11-year cycle! Nagbalhin ang magnetic force sa Adlaw, busa adunay panahon nga daghang pagbuto ug panahon nga halos wala.

copy.en:
Why do sunspots come and go?

The Sun has an 11-year cycle! At solar maximum, there are many sunspots and frequent solar flares. At solar minimum, there are very few sunspots.
copy.tl:
Bakit pumaparito at nawawala ang mga sunspot?

May 11-taong cycle ang Araw! Sa solar maximum, maraming sunspot at madalas ang solar flare. Sa solar minimum, kakaunti ang sunspot.
copy.bis:
Nganong moabot ug mawala ang mga sunspot?

Ang Adlaw adunay 11-tuig nga cycle! Sa solar maximum, daghan ang sunspot ug kanunay ang solar flare. Sa solar minimum, diyutay ang sunspot.

copy.tl: Ang lalaking sunbird ay may makinang at makukulay na balahibo na nagniningning kapag tinamaan ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang lalaki nga sunbird adunay makintab ug mabulukon nga balhibo nga mosidlak sama sa metal kung masilawan sa adlaw.

copy.en:
How do you read the time on a sundial?

You don't read the whole shadow—just its sharp edge! Look at which numbered line the edge crosses to find the time.
copy.tl:
Paano mo binabasa ang oras sa sundial?

Hindi mo binabasa ang buong anino—kundi ang matalim na gilid! Tingnan kung aling numerong linya ang tinatawid ng gilid para malaman ang oras.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbasa sa oras sa sundial?

Dili nimo basahon ang tibuok landong—kondili ang hait nga ngilit! Tan-awa kung unsang numerong linya ang tabok sa ngilit aron mahibaloan ang oras.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: which grow hard shells to protect their soft bodies

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a shell as an outer body part, but the competency requires describing outer body parts and identifying their role in movement and gathering food. The card only states the shell protects the soft body, not movement or food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: From sea snails called cowries

copy.en:
Where do sungka shells come from?

From sea snails called cowries, which grow hard shells to protect their soft bodies.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang mga sigay sa sungka?

Galing sa mga kuhol sa dagat na tinatawag na cowrie, na gumagawa ng matigas na bahay para sa kanilang malambot na katawan.
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang mga sigay sa sungka?

Gikan sa mga kuhol sa dagat nga gitawag cowrie, nga naghimo og gahi nga balay aron panalipdan ang ilang humok nga lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it still takes about 8 minutes to go from the Sun to Earth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the travel time of sunlight from the Sun to Earth. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or give their main features and composition, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How long does it take for sunlight to reach us?

Sunlight travels super fast, but it still takes about 8 minutes to go from the Sun to Earth!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal bago makarating sa atin ang liwanag ng Araw?

Mabilis ang liwanag, pero tumatagal pa rin ito ng halos 8 minuto bago makarating sa Earth mula sa Araw!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka dugay bago makaabot sa atoa ang kahayag sa Adlaw?

Dali kaayo ang kahayag, pero mga 8 ka minuto gihapon ang gidugayon aron makaabot sa Yuta gikan sa Adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they scatter heavy elements like iron across space! These pieces later build brand new stars and planets.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars and planets but does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name major celestial objects, or detail their features/composition. It focuses on supernova nucleosynthesis, which is not the subject of this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they scatter heavy elements like iron across space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the names and symbols of the first 20 or several common elements of the periodic table
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions iron as a heavy element but does not identify names and symbols of the first 20 or common elements of the periodic table. It does not teach element symbols or periodic table content.

copy.en: When huge stars explode in a giant supernova, they scatter heavy elements like iron across space! These pieces later build brand new stars and planets.
copy.tl: Kapag sumabog ang mga malalaking bituin sa isang supernova, nagkakalat sila ng mabibigat na elemento tulad ng bakal! Ang mga ito ang bubuo ng bagong bituin at planeta.
copy.bis: Kon mobuto ang dagkong bituon sa supernova, mobuga sila og bug-at nga elemento sama sa puthaw! Kining mga bahina ang moporma og bag-ong bituon ug planeta.

copy.en: In the morning, dew on leaves forms tiny round beads! This happens because surface tension pulls the water tightly together.
copy.tl: Tuwing umaga, ang hamog sa mga dahon ay nagiging maliliit na bilog na butil! Nangyayari ito dahil hinihila ng surface tension ang tubig.
copy.bis: Sa buntag, ang yamog sa mga dahon mahimong gagmay nga lingin nga butil! Nahitabo kini kay ang surface tension mobira sa tubig pagtapok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Metal is heavier than water, but a needle can float gently because surface tension holds it up!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions metal (solid) and water (liquid) but does not describe their shape or volume properties. Surface tension is not part of the G5-M-3 competency about definite/indefinite shape and volume.

copy.en: Metal is heavier than water, but a needle can float gently because surface tension holds it up!
copy.tl: Mas mabigat ang metal kaysa tubig, pero maaaring lumutang nang dahan-dahan ang karayom dahil hinahawakan ito ng surface tension!
copy.bis: Mas bug-at ang metal kay sa tubig, pero mahimong molutaw nang hinay-hinay ang dagom kay gikupot kini sa surface tension!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Surface tension pulls its thin film of water tightly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses surface tension of a liquid film, not the shape and volume properties of solids, liquids, and gases. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why does a soap bubble always stay perfectly round?

Surface tension pulls its thin film of water tightly, shaping it into the smallest possible round form!
copy.tl:
Bakit palaging nananatiling bilog ang isang bula ng sabon?

Hinihila ng surface tension ang manipis na pelikula ng tubig, hinuhubog ito sa pinakamaliit na bilog na hugis!
copy.bis:
Nganong kanunayng magpabiling lingin ang bula sa sabon?

Gibira sa surface tension ang nipis nga pelikula sa tubig, gihulma kini ngadto sa pinakagamay nga lingin nga porma!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Surface tension makes it round! It tugs the water into the smallest possible shape.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains water drop roundness via surface tension, which is a macroscopic phenomenon. It does not describe particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects as required by G7-M-3. The connection to particle attraction is implicit at best and not taught.

copy.en:
Why is a water drop round?

Surface tension makes it round! It tugs the water into the smallest possible shape.
copy.tl:
Bakit bilog ang patak ng tubig?

Dahil sa surface tension! Hinihila nito ang tubig sa pinakamaliit na hugis.
copy.bis:
Nganong lingin ang tulo sa tubig?

Tungod sa surface tension! Gibira niini ang tubig ngadto sa pinakagamay nga porma.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has one of the strongest surface tensions among common liquids
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of liquids (surface tension) but does not address shape or volume, which are the specific properties required by G5-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has one of the strongest surface tensions among common liquids

copy.en: Water is super special! It has one of the strongest surface tensions among common liquids, beating both oil and alcohol.
copy.tl: Espesyal ang tubig! Mayroon itong isa sa pinakamalakas na surface tension sa karaniwang likido, mas malakas pa kaysa langis o alkohol.
copy.bis: Espesyal ang tubig! Aduna kini usa sa pinakakusog nga surface tension taliwala sa naandang likido, mas kusog pa kay sa lana o alkohol.

copy.tl: May tatlong paraan ang mga hayop para makaligtas sa mahirap na panahon: matulog, lumipat, o magbihis at magtago.
copy.bis: Adunay tulo ka paagi ang mga mananap aron makalahutay sa lisod nga panahon: matulog, molalin, o mausab ug motago.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a flocking behavior before migration, but does not describe any change in animals to better suit their environment, nor mimicry or camouflage. It shares the broad subject of animal behavior but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Swallows often gather together in big flocks on power wires before they migrate somewhere new.
copy.tl: Madalas magtipon ang mga layang-layang nang sama-sama sa mga kawad ng kuryente bago sila lumipat ng lugar.
copy.bis: Kasagaran magtapok ang mga sayaw nga daghan sa mga kawad sa kuryente sa dili pa sila mubalhin.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water and salt mixed together but never identifies which is the solute and which is the solvent, nor does it explain their roles in a solution. It is background about sweat composition, not instruction on solute/solvent roles.

copy.en:
Why does sweat taste salty?

Because sweat is mostly water with just a little salt mixed in — that little bit of salt is what you taste!
copy.tl:
Bakit maalat ang lasa ng pawis?

Dahil halos tubig lang ang pawis na may kaunting asin — ang kaunting asin na iyon ang lasa mong maalat!
copy.bis:
Ngano parat ang lami sa singot?

Tungod kay ang singot kasagaran tubig ra nga adunay gamay nga asin — kanang gamay nga asin ang imong matilawan nga parat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Swiftlets use echolocation — making clicking sounds that bounce back to help them find their way inside dark caves!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Swiftlets use echolocation — making clicking sounds that bounce back to help them find their way inside dark caves!

copy.en:
How do swiftlets fly in pitch-dark caves?

Swiftlets use echolocation — making clicking sounds that bounce back to help them find their way inside dark caves!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakalipad ang balinsasayaw sa madilim na kweba?

Gumagamit ang balinsasayaw ng echolocation — gumagawa ito ng tunog na pumipikit-pikit para makahanap ng daan sa loob ng madilim na kweba!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglupad sa balinsasayaw sa ngitngit nga langub?

Mogamit ang balinsasayaw og echolocation — maghimo kini og tingog nga klik aron makakita og dalan sulod sa ngitngit nga langub!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they learn to click and understand the returning echoes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes echolocation in swiftlets, which involves sound production and echo reception, but the competency targets everyday sound situations like a ringing bell or hearing noises. The animal-specific echolocation is not an everyday situation and does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As they grow, they learn to click and understand the returning echoes to move around their dark cave.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a learned behavior (echolocation) that helps swiftlets navigate, but the competency focuses on animals that have changed (evolved) to better suit their environment, with examples like mimicry or camouflage. Learning to echolocate is not an evolutionary change and does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Can baby swiftlets echolocate right away?

No! Baby swiftlets can't echolocate right after hatching. As they grow, they learn to click and understand the returning echoes to move around their dark cave.
copy.tl:
Marunong ba agad mag-echolocate ang batang swiftlet?

Hindi agad! Hindi marunong mag-echolocation ang batang swiftlet pagkapisa. Habang lumalaki, natututo silang gumawa ng click at unawain ang bumabalik na tunog para makagalaw sa madilim na kweba.
copy.bis:
Makamao ba dayon mo-echolocate ang gagmayng swiftlet?

Dili dayon! Dili makamao mo-echolocate ang gagmayng swiftlet pagkahuman mapusa. Samtang nagdako sila, makakat-on sila og click ug pagsabot sa mobalik nga tingog aron makalihok sa ngitngit nga langob.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Swiftlets glue their nests, made from their own saliva, onto high cave walls or steep cliff faces!

copy.en: Swiftlets glue their nests, made from their own saliva, onto high cave walls or steep cliff faces!
copy.tl: Idinidikit ng balinsasayaw ang pugad nito, na gawa sa sarili niyang laway, sa matataas na dingding ng kweba o bangin!
copy.bis: Ang balinsasayaw magpilit sa iyang salag, nga hinimo gikan sa iyang laway, sa habog nga bongbong sa langub o pangpang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It looks bent because light changes direction, or refracts, as it passes from water into air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It looks bent because light changes direction, or refracts, as it passes from water into air!

copy.en:
Why does a stick look bent in water?

It looks bent because light changes direction, or refracts, as it passes from water into air!
copy.tl:
Bakit parang baluktot ang patpat sa tubig?

Parang baluktot siya dahil nababaluktot o nag-iiba ng direksyon ang light pagdaan mula sa tubig papunta sa hangin!
copy.bis:
Nganong morag baliko ang sungkod sa tubig?

Morag baliko siya tungod kay ang light mausab og direksyon o mag-refract samtang moagi gikan sa tubig paingon sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pendulum takes almost the exact same time for every full swing, making it super awesome at measuring time!

copy.en: A pendulum takes almost the exact same time for every full swing, making it super awesome at measuring time!
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang pendulum ng halos parehong oras sa bawat buong ugoy, kaya napakahusay niya sa pagsukat ng oras!
copy.bis: Naggamit ang pendulum og halos parehong oras sa matag bug-os nga labyog, mao nga maayo kaayo niya sukdon ang oras!
